written.description: A hunt skill for each web and API bug class, with a dispatcher that reads the scope and loads the ones that fit. Patterns from disclosed bug-bounty reports sit behind each one.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix(cbh,osint): four terminal-tooling bugs — triage gate, report BOM/CRLF, Windows console, h1 --program (#210)

* fix(cbh): triage gate — real request-target for Q1, scope-negation for Q3, clickjacking for Q7

Three false-verdict paths in the 7-Question Gate, each independently reported:

- Q1 matched a bare method word anywhere in the text, so prose like
  "target application" (contains "get ") or "input validation" passed Q1
  with no request at all. Q1 now needs a method followed by a path or URL
  (or curl / HTTP/1.1). Reported by @dajiaohuang (#209).
- Q7's never-submit list had "click-jacking" but not "clickjacking", so the
  unhyphenated spelling was never killed. Reported by @Ethereal49 (#197).
- Q3 answered YES on any scope/asset wording even when the finding itself
  said "out of scope" / "unverified". A scope/asset line carrying a negation
  no longer counts as in-scope evidence; non-scope lines ("Impact: unclear")
  still don't. Reported by @Ethereal49 (#197).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cbh): parse finding frontmatter through a leading UTF-8 BOM

A BOM (\ufeff) written by some Windows editors sits before the `---` fence,
so the `^---` frontmatter regex missed it and severity/asset fell back to
defaults. Strip a leading BOM in parse_finding_metadata, the shared chokepoint
for every command that reads a finding, not just `cbh report`.

Reported by @jazzpher (#200).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cbh): force UTF-8 stdout so Windows cp1252 consoles don't crash

cbh and setup_harness_mcp.py print the gate glyphs (check / cross / arrow /
em-dash) throughout. On a Windows console (cp1252) a bare print() raised
UnicodeEncodeError and the command died mid-run. Reconfigure stdout/stderr to
UTF-8 at both entrypoints, the same fix engine/engine.py:main already uses, so
the whole CLI is covered at one point rather than guarding every print.

Reported by @Sahilkumar-r (#180).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(offensive-osint): filter h1_reference --program by team_handle, not team_id

CompleteHacktivityReportIndex no longer accepts terms: {team_id: ...}, so
--program silently returned nothing. Switch to query_string "team_handle:<h>",
which filters correctly and still accepts sort + pagination (so --program now
composes with --top-voted / --top-bounty). Also: route the lookup progress line
to stderr so --json stdout stays pipeable, and reject an empty --program handle.

Two independent reports converged on this fix: @roonnnnyyyyyy (#206) and
@flipcyde101 (#202).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(changelog): record the four tooling bugfixes with reporter credits

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cbh,osint): review follow-ups — Q3 negation, Q1 markdown, CRLF, canonical handle

Adversarial review of the branch surfaced five real defects:

- Q3 _q3_scope_negated matched ANY line containing 'scope' plus a negation,
  so 'Impact: unclear scope of data exposure' wrongly killed an in-scope
  finding. Negation is now evaluated per line: strong phrases ('out of scope')
  disavow anywhere; weak words ('unknown','unclear') only on a scope/asset/
  target line (the key before the colon).
- Q3 negation list was space-only, so the common hyphenated 'out-of-scope'
  slipped through. Hyphens are normalized to spaces before matching.
- Q1 required whitespace between method and path, missing the markdown a PoC
  is usually written in (`GET /x`, **GET** /x, GET `/x`). The separator class
  now allows backticks and bold/italic markers. The prose ceiling
  ('an attacker can get /admin') is marked, not closed — requiring HTTP/ would
  reject the bare 'GET /path' PoC the gate must accept.
- parse_finding_metadata now also normalizes CRLF, so Windows findings (the
  same platform as the BOM in #200) don't skip frontmatter.
- h1_reference --program queried the raw input handle; query_string is
  case-sensitive while TeamLookup is not, so '--program Shopify' could return
  nothing. lookup_program now returns the team record and main uses the
  canonical handle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
